deities: Lord Krishna (Ekasarana Dharma; aniconic congregational worship at the Namghar)
festivals: Birth and death anniversaries (tithis) of Sankardev and Madhavdev

history.period: Established ~1550 AD by Madhavdeva (one satra-list gives 1539 AD — conflict flagged)
history.summary: Ganakkuchi Satra was the second satra established by Madhavdeva (Neog 2006 dates it to ~1550 AD; a Barpeta satra-listing table gives 1539 AD — the two dates conflict). While Sankardev was resident at nearby Patbaushi, Madhavdeva made Ganakkuchi his residence and composed much of his literature here — reportedly 191 Borgeets at Sankardeva's direction (Lekharu 1952) — before moving on to found Barpeta Satra. The satra lies about 1 km south of Barpeta Satra, within the Barpeta municipality. It preserves Sanchipat puthis (manuscripts), the vithis (sitting places) of Ram Ata and Ram Atoi, and items used by Madhavdeva. Coordinates are for the Ganakkuchi locality and are approximate. No reliable on-topic image was found after genuine searching; a placeholder image slot is intentionally left empty.

name: Ganakkuchi Satra
town_description: Barpeta is the headquarters town of Barpeta district in Lower Assam, about 95-130 km northwest of Guwahati. Known as the 'Satra Nagari' (town of satras), it grew around Madhavdeva's Barpeta Satra and its twenty-two hatis, and remains the historic centre of the Ekasarana Vaishnavite tradition, with handloom weaving and bell-metal work as local crafts.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati (approx. 95-130 km; ~2.5-3 hours by road).
travel.railway: Barpeta Road (Simlaguri) station, approx. 13-14 km from the town.
travel.road: Ganakkuchi lies ~1 km south of Barpeta Satra within Barpeta town; reached by auto/taxi from Barpeta town centre or Barpeta Road.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Doul Utsav season (February-March) for festival culture.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Like the other Barpeta satras it is open daily for morning and evening prayers; traditionally only men are permitted inside the Namghar. The exact daily schedule is not published online — verify locally before travel.
